paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: The line plot, titled “Answer Change Percentage by Initial Accuracy,” illustrates the average percentage change in answers across seven turns for a language model (Claude on MMLU-Pro), segmented by whether the initial answer was correct or incorrect. The x-axis, labeled “Turn Number,” is linear and ranges from 1 to 7, with integer tick marks at each turn. The y-axis, labeled “Average Change Percentage (%)”, is also linear, ranging from 0 to 50, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 10. Two lines are plotted: the red line with circular markers represents “Initial Correct Answer,” starting at approximately 4% at Turn 1, rising slightly to 6% at Turn 2, dipping to 6% again at Turn 3, then jumping to 12% at Turn 4, and remaining flat at 12% through Turns 5 to 7. The orange line with circular markers represents “Initial Incorrect Answer,” beginning at 17% at Turn 1, rising to 25% at Turn 2, holding steady at 25% at Turn 3, then sharply increasing to 49% at Turn 4, and remaining constant at 49% through Turns 5 to 7. The plot visually confirms the caption’s claim that models with initially incorrect answers exhibit substantially higher answer change percentages—peaking at nearly 50%—compared to those with initially correct answers, which stabilize around 12%.
